title: What is inside a web project
desc: A project is a folder with a few well-known places in it. Knowing what each one is for makes any new project easy to read.

root.name: my-app/
root.text: The project folder. Everything below lives here.

rows.name: src/
rows.text: The code you write. Most of your time is spent here.

rows.name: public/
rows.text: Files sent to the browser as they are: images, icons, fonts.

rows.name: tests/
rows.text: Small programs that check the code still works.

rows.name: docs/
rows.text: Notes for people: how to start, how it is built.

rows.name: package.json
rows.text: The shopping list: which libraries the project needs.

rows.name: README.md
rows.text: The front door: what this is and how to run it.

rows.name: .env
rows.text: Secrets such as passwords. Never shared, never uploaded.

note: Folder names end with a slash. Names with a dot are files. Order here is only for reading; real folders are listed alphabetically.
